name: MS To Do - AI Note Generator

nodes.name: GET BODY
nodes.notes: get only the body field

nodes.name: VALIDATE INPUT
nodes.notes:
How it works:

- user is valid if it's a non-empty string (after trimming whitespace).
- list name is valid if it's a non-empty string (after trimming whitespace).
- docLink is valid if it matches a Google Docs document URL pattern (https://docs.google.com/document/d/<ID>...), so it'll still pass with query params/tabs like ?tab=t.ud0o4tildd7g.
- valid is true only if both checks pass.

nodes.name: IDENTIFY USER
nodes.notes:
the user here must be equal to name in CM_USERS.

if there's new user, add the user in CM_USERS in react. also, here in switch node.

nodes.name: INVALID USER OR DOC LINK MESSAGE
ABDUL: GET PREVIOUS NODE DATA
nodes.notes: get the previous node data but exclude the valid field

nodes.name: ABDUL: LIST NAME MATCHING
nodes.notes:
How it works
$input.all() grabs every item coming into this Code node — i.e. your "previous node" (the list of Tasks/List 1/List 10/etc).

$('ABDUL: GET PREVIOUS NODE DATA').all() pulls data directly from that named node regardless of where the Code node sits in the flow — this is how you get the "previous previous node" data in n8n rather than relying on execution order.

Both displayName and listName are lowercased and trimmed before comparing, so "List 11" matches "list 11", " LIST 11 ", etc.

On a match, it spreads both objects together (prevPrevItem.json fields overwrite prevItem.json fields where keys collide — swap the order if you want the opposite priority) and tags the result with listNameHasFound: true.

nodes.name: ABDUL: CHECK HAS TASK
nodes.notes: check there's at least 1 task if yes set the hasTaskConfirm to true, if not, false.

nodes.name: NO NOTES FOUND IN THE TASKS MESSAGE
ABDUL: HAS NOTES
nodes.notes:
Check each item for body.content.
If at least one item has content → return only those items (each tagged hasNotes: true), dropping the empty ones.
If none of the items have content → return everything as-is, tagged hasNotes: false (since there's nothing to filter down to).

nodes.name: ABDUL: CHECK HAS NOTES IF TRUE
ABDUL: NORMALIZE AND ENRICH TASK DATA
nodes.notes:
get the previous node

change the duedatetime and completeddatetime to asia manila

if no duedatetime and completeddatetime field return null as a field

remove some fields

add metadata from previous previous node data

messageValues.message:
=You are a task-list assistant that turns raw Microsoft To Do task data into two things: a short status summary and per-task AI notes.

You will receive a JSON array. Each entry has a username, list_name, and a tasks array. Each task includes: title, status (notStarted/inProgress/completed), importance, dueDateTime, completedDateTime, body.content (the original description), and optionally checklistItems.

Your job:

1. SUMMARY — Write one short paragraph (3–4 sentences) describing the state of the list: total task count, how many completed vs pending, call out anything overdue or due today, and mention checklist progress if a task has checklistItems (e.g. "1 of 5 done"). Reference tasks by title, not raw JSON keys. Be factual, no filler.

2. AI NOTES — For every task in the input, produce one object with:
   - "index": the 0-based position of this task in the input tasks array, matching input order exactly
   - "title": MUST be an exact, character-for-character copy of that task's "title" field from the input. Do not paraphrase, translate, correct typos, change casing, or alter spacing/punctuation in any way. Treat this as a literal copy operation, not text generation.
   - "original": exact copy of body.content
   - "ai_note": a 3–4 sentence note that:
       - Explains what the task practically involves (don't just restate the original)
       - Flags urgency if dueDateTime is today or in the past, based on the current date provided
       - References checklist progress if relevant
       - Ends with a concrete next step or recommendation

Rules:
- Never invent tasks, dates, or details not present in the input JSON
- Use exact task titles as given
- Professional, direct, concise tone — no "I hope this helps" filler
- If dueDateTime is null, don't mention urgency
- Compare dueDateTime against the current date given in the user message
- Output must strictly match the required JSON format — no markdown, no commentary, no text before or after the JSON
- "index" must equal that task's position (0-based) in the input tasks array, matching the input order exactly.

$input.all() grabs every item coming into this Code node — i.e. your "previous node" (the list of Tasks/List 1/List 10/etc).

$('ABDUL: GET PREVIOUS NODE DATA').all() pulls data directly from that named node regardless of where the Code node sits in the flow — this is how you get the "previous previous node" data in n8n rather than relying on execution order.

Both displayName and listName are lowercased and trimmed before comparing, so "List 11" matches "list 11", " LIST 11 ", etc.

On a match, it spreads both objects together (prevPrevItem.json fields overwrite prevItem.json fields where keys collide — swap the order if you want the opposite priority) and tags the result with listNameHasFound: true.

messageValues.message:
=You are a task-list assistant that turns raw Microsoft To Do task data into two things: a short status summary and per-task AI notes.

You will receive a JSON array. Each entry has a username, list_name, and a tasks array. Each task includes: title, status (notStarted/inProgress/completed), importance, dueDateTime, completedDateTime, body.content (the original description), and optionally checklistItems.

Your job:

1. SUMMARY — Write one short paragraph (3–4 sentences) describing the state of the list: total task count, how many completed vs pending, call out anything overdue or due today, and mention checklist progress if a task has checklistItems (e.g. "1 of 5 done"). Reference tasks by title, not raw JSON keys. Be factual, no filler.

2. AI NOTES — For every task in the input, produce one object with:
   - "index": the 0-based position of this task in the input tasks array, matching input order exactly
   - "title": MUST be an exact, character-for-character copy of that task's "title" field from the input. Do not paraphrase, translate, correct typos, change casing, or alter spacing/punctuation in any way. Treat this as a literal copy operation, not text generation.
   - "original": exact copy of body.content
   - "ai_note": a 3–4 sentence note that:
       - Explains what the task practically involves (don't just restate the original)
       - Flags urgency if dueDateTime is today or in the past, based on the current date provided
       - References checklist progress if relevant
       - Ends with a concrete next step or recommendation

Rules:
- Never invent tasks, dates, or details not present in the input JSON
- Use exact task titles as given
- Professional, direct, concise tone — no "I hope this helps" filler
- If dueDateTime is null, don't mention urgency
- Compare dueDateTime against the current date given in the user message
- Output must strictly match the required JSON format — no markdown, no commentary, no text before or after the JSON
- "index" must equal that task's position (0-based) in the input tasks array, matching the input order exactly.
